name: Kiwi Green
lede: Kiwi Green is a bright, yellow-leaning green named for the kiwifruit's flesh, brighter than our library's plain Kiwi entry for the same fruit.

sections.title: Brighter than the fruit it is named for
sections.body:
Our library holds a separate, plainer entry for [[kiwi|Kiwi]], and the two sit close but not identical, about 5 units apart in CIEDE2000, with Kiwi Green the more saturated of the pair [1]. Both come from the 2010 xkcd color survey, and the survey's log does not say why two distinct crowd clusters formed for what is nominally the same fruit [1].

The kiwifruit's actual flesh color runs duller and more olive than either survey entry, closer to the skin of an unripe lime than to this swatch's full brightness [2]. ISCC-NBS 1955 would file Kiwi Green as a brilliant yellow green, and its nearest named relatives are [[chartreuse|Chartreuse]] and [[lime-green|Lime Green]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, holds no painting where this exact bright green covers five percent or more of the canvas [4]. A green this saturated and this light sits outside the range aged oil paint and varnish typically produce [4]. A match would be a computed color comparison, never a pigment identification [4].
